title: Workforce engagement
blurb: Native WEM and Verint, the roster, quality, surveys, and the recording clock.
summary: WEM tells you who should be there. The dialer should believe the schedule. Recordings do not last by hope.

lessons.title: Five9 WEM and a Verint path both exist
objectives: List the pieces in the contract
paragraphs: The workforce page says Five9 offers WEM natively and also partners with vendors such as Verint so a customer can fit the suite they already run. It says Five9 manages installation, configuration, maintenance, and upgrades for the WEM solution they deliver.

Do not tell a floor they are 'on Verint' or 'on native WEM' without looking. The page says both exist. Recording, QM, analytics, WFM, surveys, and CRM connectors are the pieces the data sheet says you integrate.
uncertain: This lab does not know which suite a given customer bought. The product page says both native WEM and partners such as Verint are offered.

lessons.title: Workforce management is the roster
objectives: Feed the dialer from the schedule
paragraphs: WFM, in the product language, is how you staff to the work: schedules, intraday changes, adherence. It is not the dialer mode and not the service level target, though it exists so those can be met.
A predictive book that uses headcount instead of the schedule will overdial at every planned break. The roster is an input to the mode you already chose.

lessons.title: Quality management listens on purpose
objectives: Match the form to the queue
Remember hold is in the recording
paragraphs: The product page describes multi-channel evaluations, desktop monitoring, and automated scoring. The desktop page says agents can review evaluations without leaving Plus. That is QM: a sample of work, a score, a conversation with the person.

A 100 percent score on a form nobody respects is not quality. The form has to match the call the customer had. Recording is the evidence. The EULA says recordings include hold and what happens after a transfer, and that the customer must meet notice and consent laws.

lessons.title: Analytics and surveys sit beside the call
objectives: Keep survey, abandon, and topics apart
paragraphs: The data sheet and the product page put interaction analytics and customer surveys next to QM and WFM. Analytics is how you see topics across many calls. A survey is how the customer scores the one call. They are not the abandon rate and they are not a disposition, unless you deliberately map them.
This lab does not claim a specific analytics vendor screen. Native WEM and a partner suite will not look identical. The question to ask is which topics you will act on.

lessons.title: Recordings expire
objectives: Do not promise a recording past the clock
paragraphs: The retention page says VCC audio recordings are kept for the sooner of 30 days or a successful SFTP or FTP offload, or as the contract says. E911 call recordings are listed at 30 days. Agent data is 60 days. Campaign state is 120 days. Disabled domains are listed at 120 days after closure. DIDs and toll-free numbers are listed at 90 days after closure.
If you need a call from last quarter, the offload had to succeed. A failed SFTP job is a silent deletion clock. QM cannot score what is already gone.
uncertain: Contracts can override the published table. Read the agreement for the domain you are in.

lessons.title: The agent should not need a second login
objectives: Put WEM actions where the agent already works
paragraphs: The desktop page's point is that schedules, adherence, time off, shift bidding, and evaluations are reachable in Plus and, through connectors, in the CRM. A second password for WEM is a design smell if the connector was in the contract.
Shift bidding is named on that page. This lab does not reproduce the bidding rules. If bidding exists, the result still has to become the schedule the dialer respects.
uncertain: Bidding rules are suite-specific and were not copied from a manual.

lessons.title: What this lab will not pretend to run
objectives: Keep the lab and the tenant apart
paragraphs: This lab has no live WEM tenant. You cannot approve a real time-off request here. You can say which product page promised the button, which retention clock will delete the evidence, and which dialer mistake a bad roster causes.
That is the useful line between a simulator and a system of record. The pacing bench is a classroom. The schedule in the customer's suite is the roster. The campaign dialog is the mode.
